Silence and lock the phone itself

Fovea runs in the browser, so it cannot silence your phone or stop you leaving the app. Your phone can do both, and it puts everything back as it was when you switch them off. Menu names can differ a little between phones.

iPhone and iPad

  • Silence: open Control Centre, tap Focus, then Do Not Disturb. Tap the three dots beside it to choose "For 1 hour" so it ends by itself.
  • Lock to this app, set up once: Settings, Accessibility, Guided Access. Turn it on and set a passcode under Passcode Settings.
  • Each session: with Fovea open, triple-click the side button and tap Start. To leave, triple-click again and enter the passcode.

Android

  • Silence: swipe down from the top and tap Do Not Disturb. To have it end by itself, choose a length in Settings, Modes, Do Not Disturb, Duration for Quick Settings.
  • Lock to this app, set up once: Settings, Security, Advanced, App pinning. Turn it on.
  • Each session: open the recent apps view, tap Fovea's icon above its preview, and tap Pin. To leave, swipe up and hold, or hold Back and Overview, then enter your PIN.

Where these sounds come from

The nature sounds are recordings their makers released to the public domain, softened for long listening. Mountain breeze: felix.blume and keweldog. Light rain: barkenov. Soft thunderstorm: the same rain with thunder by Ben Burnes and rubberduck. Fire crackling: ezwa. Birds in the forest: a wood thrush recorded by kvgarlic. Bamboo forest: the breeze recordings with generated bamboo knocks. Meditation bowls, the 432 Hz tone and white noise are generated by the app.

How the training works

  1. Warm up with one drill. Each drill below isolates a single attention skill and gives one score. Most take about a minute.
  2. Hold a session at your current length.
  3. Let the length grow. Three clean sessions in a row add 5 minutes. Two rough ones in a row take 5 minutes off, so the target stays within reach.
  4. Check what broke it. The Progress page shows what pulls you away and the hours you focus best.

A clean session is one you finish as planned, with two or fewer distractions and a focus rating of 4 or 5. A rough one is ended early, has five or more distractions, or is rated 1 or 2. Drill scores rise with practice, so treat them as a warm-up and a trend. The real measure of progress is the session length you can hold.

High-quality focus counts the minutes in clean sessions: finished as planned, with two or fewer distractions and a focus rating of 4 or 5.
